questions.stem: ___ is rotted plant waste that makes soil rich.
questions.explanation: Compost is made when plant waste such as peels and leaves rots. It adds goodness to the soil.

questions.stem: Match each of the three Rs to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less, reuse means use things again, and recycle means turn old things into new ones.

questions.stem: Sort each waste into solid, liquid or gas.
questions.explanation: Food scraps and plastic are solids. Dirty water is a liquid. Smoke and the carbon dioxide we breathe out are gases.

questions.stem: Which of these can be composted? Choose all that are right.
options: fruit and vegetable peels
dead leaves
egg shells
a plastic bag
a metal can
questions.explanation: Plant and food waste rots and becomes compost. Plastic and metal do not rot, so they do not belong in a compost pit.

questions.stem: A plastic bag buried in the soil will rot away within a few weeks.
questions.explanation: Plastic does not rot. A plastic bag buried for four weeks shows no change, so it stays in the environment for a very long time.

questions.stem: The oxygen that plants release is a gas waste that is useful to us.
questions.explanation: Plants give out oxygen as a waste gas, and we need it to breathe. Not all waste is harmful.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to show how a community makes compost.
sequence: Workers collect food and vegetable waste from homes.
The waste is piled in boxes at a compost plant.
Worms and microbes break the waste down.
After about two months it becomes dark, crumbly compost.
Farmers and gardeners use the compost on their soil.
questions.explanation: Food waste rots easily, so decomposers such as worms and microbes turn it into compost. Less rubbish goes to the dump and farmers get good soil.

questions.stem: Which is an example of **reusing**?
options: giving old paper to the bhangari collector
using an old jar as a pencil pot
buying food with less packaging
making peels into compost
questions.explanation: Reuse means using something again, so a jar can become a pencil pot. Giving paper to a collector is recycling, buying less packaging is reducing, and peels make compost.

questions.stem: Taking a cloth bag to the shop is an example of…
options: reducing waste
recycling waste
burning waste
composting waste
questions.explanation: A cloth bag can be used many times, so you use fewer plastic bags. Using less is called reducing.

questions.stem: How can plastic bags cause floods in a city?
questions.model_answer: They block the drains, so rain water cannot flow away.
questions.explanation: Plastic bags do not rot. They collect in drains and stop rain water flowing away, so the streets flood.

questions.stem: Why is compost good for a garden?
options: It makes the soil hard like a brick.
It stops rain from falling on plants.
It keeps all the worms away.
It makes soil rich for plants.
questions.explanation: Compost adds goodness to the soil, so plants get what they need to grow well.

questions.stem: Rubbish heaps attract rats and flies that can spread disease.
questions.explanation: Rats and flies live and feed on rubbish. They can carry germs, so piles of waste can make people ill.

questions.stem: To reduce is to use ___. To reuse is to use things ___.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less. Reuse means use the same thing again instead of throwing it away.

questions.stem: Animals breathe out a waste gas called ___.
questions.explanation: Animals breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide. Plants use carbon dioxide to make their food.

questions.stem: Dirty water from factories can pollute rivers like the Buriganga.
questions.explanation: Factory waste water often carries chemicals. When it flows into a river it pollutes the water and harms fish and the people who use the river.

questions.stem: Sort the pictures into compost, recycle or reuse.
questions.explanation: Peels and leaves rot into compost. Paper and metal cans can be made into new things. A cloth bag and old clothes can be used again.

questions.stem: Which picture shows waste that can be composted?
questions.explanation: A banana peel is plant waste. It rots and turns into compost. Plastic, metal and glass do not rot.

questions.stem: Which picture shows a gas waste from vehicles?
questions.explanation: Exhaust fumes are gas waste. Spilled oil is a liquid, and a bottle and a banana peel are solids.

questions.stem: Match each picture to the kind of waste it shows.
questions.explanation: A bottle is a solid, oil is a liquid and smoke is a gas. Factories and vehicles make all three kinds of waste.

questions.stem: Which picture shows a good way to reduce waste when shopping?
questions.explanation: A cloth bag can be used again and again, so you need fewer plastic bags. Lots of packaging and new bottles make more waste.

questions.stem: After heavy rain a street in Dhaka floods because plastic bags block the drain. What is the best long-term fix?
options: Use fewer plastic bags and bin used ones.
Burn the bags at the side of the street.
Throw the bags into the river instead.
Wait for the rain to stop falling.
questions.explanation: Using fewer bags and binning the rest stops plastic reaching drains. Burning makes smoke, and rivers are polluted by plastic too.

questions.stem: Mina's family has vegetable peels every day. What is the best thing to do with them?
options: Throw them into the river.
Put them in a compost pit.
Burn them near the house.
Put them with the plastic for recycling.
questions.explanation: Vegetable peels rot and become compost, which makes soil rich for plants. Rivers and the air should not be polluted.

questions.stem: Lina's family wants to give things to the bhangari collector for recycling. Which can they give? Choose all that are right.
options: old newspapers
empty metal cans
some plastic bottles
banana peels
questions.explanation: Paper, metal and some plastic can be made into new things. Banana peels are best for compost.

questions.stem: Arif's neighbour burns a pile of rubbish behind the house. What is the problem?
options: The smoke makes the air unhealthy.
The fire makes the rubbish disappear safely.
The smoke cleans the air.
The ashes will turn into compost.
questions.explanation: Smoke from burning rubbish is gas waste. It makes the air unhealthy to breathe, so it is better to compost, reuse or recycle.

questions.stem: Class 3B buried four things for four weeks. Banana peel: mostly gone. Paper: soft and falling apart. Plastic bag: no change. Metal bottle cap: no change, a little rust. Which conclusion is best?
options: Everything rots completely in four weeks.
Metal rots faster than paper does in soil.
Plant waste rots; plastic and metal do not.
Plastic bags rot faster than banana peels do.
questions.explanation: The banana peel and the paper came from plants, and decomposers broke them down. Plastic and metal showed no change, so they stay in the environment for a very long time.

questions.stem: Why is a plastic bag in a river a bigger problem than a banana peel?
questions.model_answer: Plastic does not rot, so it stays for a very long time and can harm fish and turtles. A banana peel rots away.
questions.explanation: A banana peel rots and becomes part of the soil. Plastic does not rot, so it keeps polluting and can harm animals or block drains.

questions.stem: In an example neighbourhood, 40 families each make 2 kg of food waste a day. All of it is made into compost. How much food waste is kept out of the dump in 5 days?
options: 80 kg
200 kg
400 kg
10 kg
questions.explanation: 40 families × 2 kg = 80 kg every day. Over 5 days that is 80 × 5 = 400 kg. 80 kg is only one day.

questions.stem: Imran says, "Smoke from a fire is not waste because it just disappears into the air." What is the best reply?
options: Smoke is useful waste, just like the oxygen from plants.
Smoke is solid waste, so it can be recycled easily.
Smoke is only waste if you can see it clearly.
Smoke is gas waste, and it makes the air unhealthy.
questions.explanation: Smoke does not disappear: it spreads through the air and can harm our breathing. Smoke from fires, vehicles and factories is gas waste.
